scope.flow: ERC-4337 UserOp validation for an unclaimed AtomWallet via AtomWallet.owner() and _validateSignature
scope.environment: ERC-4337 account abstraction with ERC-7562-compliant bundlers; AtomWallet and MultiVault contracts

statements.text: The AtomWallet has isClaimed == false, so ownership is delegated to multiVault.getAtomWarden().
A UserOp is submitted for the unclaimed AtomWallet and reaches validateUserOp during the validation phase.
During _validateSignature, owner() is invoked and, in the unclaimed branch, makes an external call to multiVault.getAtomWarden().
multiVault.getAtomWarden() reads the walletConfig.atomWarden storage slot in MultiVault's storage.
A compliant bundler simulates the UserOp and checks the validation phase's external storage reads.

The walletConfig.atomWarden slot holds the warden address, not the AtomWallet address, and was not derived from keccak(atomWalletAddress || ...), so the storage read is not associated with the calling AtomWallet.

During the ERC-4337 validation phase, an account's validation must only read external-contract storage slots associated with that account (value equals the account or derived as keccak(account || x) + n), per ERC-7562 STO-021/STO-022.
A UserOp for an unclaimed AtomWallet whose validation reads only associated storage should not be rejected at simulation by an ERC-7562-compliant bundler.
Every UserOp submitted for the wallet will be rejected at simulation by any ERC-7562-compliant bundler
The wallet cannot be used as an ERC-4337 smart account until claimed.
The ATOM_WARDEN — the party responsible for acting on behalf of unclaimed atoms — is also blocked from submitting UserOps on those atoms via standard bundling infrastructure.
this effectively disables ERC-4337 functionality for every newly created atom.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the UserOp is actually submitted in a real transaction; rejection is described as a conditional simulation outcome.
Report does not specify the exact caller/actor submitting the UserOp beyond the wallet being unclaimed.
The claim that all unclaimed wallets are affected is a scope generalization, not a per-transaction precondition.
